description.md: How to get help with Photivra Nope Camera, report a problem, and check which devices it runs on.

intro.md: Photivra Nope Camera has no accounts and makes no network connections, so it can’t send us a report, and we can’t see what happened on your device. To get help, write to us in one of these ways.

issueHeading.md: Report a problem or ask a question

issue.md: [Open an issue on GitHub](https://github.com/Photivra/nope-camera/issues). You need a free GitHub account.

issueNote.md: Issues are public. Don’t include personal information, and attach a photo only if you’re willing to make it public: a photo can carry its location and other details.

emailNote.md: If you write, your message and your email address are forwarded to us by Cloudflare Email Routing and stored by our email provider. We use them only to answer you. We delete messages after 1 year, and sooner if you ask.

security.md: Use [private vulnerability reporting](https://github.com/Photivra/nope-camera/security/advisories/new) on GitHub. Please don’t open a public issue for a security problem.

include1.md: The app version, from Settings, then About.

include2.md: Your device model and its iOS or iPadOS version.

include3.md: What you did, what you expected, and what happened instead.

tested.md: For version 1.0.0 the app was run on real hardware on an iPhone 16 Pro Max and an iPad Air (5th generation). On other models, on iOS and iPadOS 26, and on Apple Watch, it was run only in Apple’s Simulator, which has no real camera. If something on these pages isn’t true on your device, tell us: it’s handled as a bug.

a11y.md: What the app has for VoiceOver, Voice Control, Switch Control, a keyboard and large text, and what has and hasn’t been checked, is on the [accessibility page](/accessibility/). A problem with any of them is handled as a bug: report it in the same way.

a.md: Into your photo library. The app saves each photo straight to Photos and stores no copy of its own.

q.md: Why can’t the app show my older photos?

a.md: The app can only add photos to your library. iOS doesn’t let it see your existing photos.
That lens can’t save unprocessed RAW. The app tells you before you shoot, unless you turn that marker off, and labels the photo.

q.md: How can I check that the app makes no network connections?

a.md: Turn on App Privacy Report in Settings, under Privacy & Security. It lists every domain an app contacts. The app should list none.
Whether the file has changed since it was signed. It is not proof of who took the photo. Signing is off by default.
